description: Blocks STARTING a heavy operation (VS Code extension rebuild/`vsce package`, a multi-model `review diff`/`quorum`/`brainstorm`/`just-ask` pass, a build/test-suite run, or a GPU model load: stt, whisper-cli, whisper-server, llama-cli, llama-server, mlx_lm/mlx_whisper, or any command handed a .bin/.gguf/.ggml/.safetensors model file) while the machine is short of memory. Any one signal blocks. macOS: (1) `sysctl kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level` >= RIG_HEAVY_OP_BLOCK_AT_LEVEL (default 2; 1=normal/2=warn/4=critical); (2) from `vm_stat`: wired share of RAM above RIG_HEAVY_OP_MAX_WIRED_PCT (default 75) or free + inactive + speculative + purgeable below RIG_HEAVY_OP_MIN_AVAILABLE_MB (default 512). Linux (calibrated on the 2026-10-10/11 thrash of a shared 48 GB / 16 GB-swap workstation: three concurrent review fan-outs plus docker-backed suites lost 26 GB in two minutes on a full swap, the kernel OOM never fired, manual reset): /proc/meminfo MemAvailable below RIG_HEAVY_OP_MIN_AVAILABLE_MB (default max(8192, 20% of MemTotal)); /proc/pressure/memory `some avg10` above RIG_HEAVY_OP_MAX_PSI_SOME10 (default 10); a memory budget that does not cover the new op: MemAvailable minus, for each heavy runner already live, max(0, expected cost - its tree PSS from smaps_rollup, or the largest single RSS where PSS is unreadable), minus the new op's expected cost, below RIG_HEAVY_OP_HEADROOM_MB (default 4096; costs RIG_HEAVY_OP_COST_REVIEW_MB 3072 per review run (measured peak p95 1125 MB, max 3195 MB over 294 runs), RIG_HEAVY_OP_COST_DOCKER_MB 8192 per docker build, RIG_HEAVY_OP_COST_SUITE_MB 3072 otherwise); SwapFree below RIG_HEAVY_OP_MIN_SWAP_FREE_PCT of SwapTotal (default 30) only while that budget leaves less than 2x the headroom (unconditionally when the scan is unavailable); or at least RIG_HEAVY_OP_MAX_LIVE (hard ceiling, default 5) heavy runners already live. Live runners come from a stateless /proc scan for pytest, bun test, vitest, jest, mypy, tsc -b, cargo test, go test, make test|check, docker build and `review` processes with their claude/codex/opencode seats (one per review), one per runner tree, each listed in the block message with pid, tree PSS, its reservation and its omp session (topmost omp ancestor, titled via `tg-ctl omp-live status --json`, the source of `omp-steer list`); real `server-run` trees are not counted and `server-run -- <cmd>` is not a heavy op when the program resolves to the installed server-offload script (~/.agents/skills/server-offload/server-run, or this checkout's copy or one in its registered git worktrees; no relative path, and no function or alias definition, PATH assignment or `hash -p` in the same command). A `review` pass run by the installed review-cli (the checkout ~/.local/bin/review resolves to, or one of its registered git worktrees) whose own reviewlib.admission.load_settings() reports admission enabled (review-cli#614), in a command that neither mentions REVIEW_ADMISSION nor prefixes the review with an assignment or env option, is queued by review-cli itself: the budget, swap and live-runner ceiling are skipped for it, the emergency signals (MemAvailable floor, PSI, wired share, jetsam level) still block; same anti-spoofing rules as server-run. Added after 2026-08-27/28 (concurrent heavy agent work drove free memory to ~65MB and hung VS Code windows), 2026-09-29 (13 concurrent whisper-cli runs wired 95.7% of a 24GB Mac into GPU buffers at NORMAL jetsam pressure and kernel-panicked it) and 2026-10-10/11 (above). A GPU model load is also refused at once while every slot of the machine-wide GPU slot pool (lib/agenttools_gpu_slots: flock lock files, RIG_GPU_SLOTS default 2, freed by the kernel when a holder dies) is taken; the same load queued through `python3 <agent-tools>/lib/agenttools_gpu_slots run -- <cmd>` is not refused, since that wrapper waits for a slot itself. The hook never waits and keeps no state of its own: it re-reads memory, swap, pressure, the process table and the kernel-managed slot locks on every call, so nothing can leak or deadlock and a retry after they free up passes. No self-bypass and no Telegram hatch-escalation (an objective, self-resolving fact, not a human judgment call); applies to the orchestrator and subagents alike. Fails open when no memory signal is readable and skips only the slot check when the slot lib is missing: an availability circuit-breaker, not a security boundary. on_error=open.
